clue.text: It indicates disapproval of little Tom's county

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the folk tale, so little Tom's gives his surname with the possessive
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A remark that some small boy's home county gets the thumbs-down.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is the thumb-sized boy of English folklore; County Down is in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The gesture of pointing the thumb downward signals rejection, as in the Roman arena.

clue.text: Success taking that woman to this position

parts.note: a hit is a success, as with a hit record
her refers to a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: Someone's triumph carries a woman into her present post.
explanation.definitionFit: The old adverb means towards this place, as in come over here.

clue.text: Menagerie leader more dexterous when catching a tiger, perhaps

indicators.note: catching means holding something within, so the letter a is put inside the other pieces
a leader comes at the front, so the opening letter of menagerie is taken

parts.note: neater means more deft or skilful with the hands

explanation.surface: The boss of a zoo shows extra skill in capturing a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts A between M (the first letter of Menagerie) and NEATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger that has taken to killing people is called by this name; the clue's 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Demonstrate garment for an equestrian competitor

parts.note: to show something is to demonstrate it
a jumper is the British word for a knitted sweater

explanation.surface: Showing off a piece of clothing made for a rider at a horse event.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a jumper is a pullover sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider who competes in jumping horses over fences in an arena is an equestrian contestant.

clue.text: Unconventional position of copper given desk job

definitions.text: position of copper given desk job
definitions.meaning: a policeman put behind a desk is no longer patrolling his street route

explanation.definitionFit: Unusual or quirky things depart from the regular rhythm; a desk-bound policeman has left his patrol round.

clue.text: It secures a climbing plant, mostly

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means reading upwards, so the shortened plant name is turned round
mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a liana is a woody climbing vine of tropical forests

explanation.surface: Something fastens a creeper that is growing upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts LIANA to LIAN, and 'climbing' turns that upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal spike hammered in fastens things together, holding them firmly in place.

clue.text: Score-book?

parts.note: read not as a tally of points but as the written words that go with a musical score, as for an opera

explanation.definitionFit: The text of an opera, printed as a booklet, accompanies the musical score.

clue.text: Plant having poison — and no label, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of the fodder are jumbled

explanation.surface: A poisonous plant has gone without a warning tag, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the ten letters of AND NO LABEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly nightshade is a toxic herb whose berries contain atropine.

clue.text: Counsel links retiring US lawyer with depravity

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the lawyer's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor
vice is wickedness or depravity

explanation.surface: A barrister links a retreating American attorney to corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counsel' looks like a lawyer, tying in with the US lawyer, but it means guidance; 'retiring' reverses the attorney's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel as a noun is guidance or recommendation given to someone.

clue.text: Deadlock created when teachers protect corrupt don

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a school's teachers are its staff

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or altered, so the letters of don are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stalemate arises when schoolteachers shield a crooked university lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deadlock' is not a hairstyle or a lock but an impasse; 'corrupt' rearranges the don's letters and 'protect' wraps the teachers round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A standoff is an impasse where neither side will give ground.

clue.text: Castle dance mostly conforming to accepted standards

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
moral means in line with accepted standards of conduct

explanation.surface: A castle's dances are mostly proper and respectable affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims BALL to BAL. BALMORAL is the British royal family's castle in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral is the royal estate and castle in Aberdeenshire, Scotland.

clue.text: Card carrying royal summons

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the letter for royal goes within the other piece

parts.note: a card is a witty, amusing person, a wit
R is a standard abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: A playing card bears a royal command to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' is not a playing card but a joker of a person, a WIT, with R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal writ is a formal written order, such as one commanding someone to appear in court.

clue.text: Retirement money taken from account

definitions.meaning: a pulling back or retreat, as of troops
cash taken out of a bank account

explanation.definitionFit: Retreat from a position and removal of cash from the bank both share this noun.

clue.text: Like deed when sent back? It's natural

definitions.meaning: the word deed reads the same backwards, so reversing it changes nothing

explanation.definitionFit: A palindrome is unchanged by reversal; a natural manner is free of affectation.

clue.text: Just the reason for popular entertainment

parts.note: just means fair and even-handed
grounds are the reason for doing something, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: Simply the motive behind mass amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' reads as 'simply', but it is the adjective fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A site with rides, stalls and sideshows stands, by metonymy, for amusements for the masses.

clue.text: Least amount those in authority will accept for treatment

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: they is the vague pronoun for the powers that be, as in they say
a rap is the least bit, as in not care a rap

explanation.surface: The minimum the authorities will take in payment for medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: The pronoun stands for the anonymous authorities of 'they won't allow it'; 'will accept' takes the least amount inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is remedial care for an illness or disorder.

clue.text: Excited cow initially not jumping over the moon

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words before it

parts.note: static means motionless, not leaping about

explanation.surface: A thrilled cow that is not, after all, leaping over the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes E and C from Excited and cow; 'Excited' looks like the definition but is only fodder. The surface plays on the nursery rhyme cow that jumped over the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the moon is a British idiom for delighted, thrilled.

clue.text: Get parted from one's sweetheart in commotion

indicators.note: in places the middle pieces within the word for commotion

parts.note: a din is a loud noise or commotion
one is I, and 's stands for is, giving I is read as IS
jo is an old Scots word for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: Being separated from one's beloved amid all the uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', the letter I then S. 'in' puts those and the sweetheart inside the commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To disjoin is to separate or come apart.

clue.text: Oriental father overwhelmed by girl's energy

indicators.note: overwhelmed means engulfed, so the father's letters sit inside the girl's name

parts.note: Jane's is a girl's name with the possessive
pa is an informal word for father
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An Eastern parent is swamped by a young woman's vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwhelmed by' puts the father inside the girl's name, with the energy symbol after.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something from Japan is Eastern in the old sense of oriental.

clue.text: Essentials for Henry Higgins, initially — but not Eliza

definitions.text: Essentials for Henry Higgins, initially — but not Eliza

parts.words: Essentials for Henry Higgins, initially — but not Eliza
parts.note: Henry Higgins begins with two letters H; Eliza Doolittle in Pygmalion and My Fair Lady drops that letter in her Cockney speech

explanation.definitionFit: The name of the letter H is spelt out as a word; plural for the two initials.

clue.text: Tasteful record making money, though not accepted at first

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: not means without, so the chosen letter is removed

parts.note: earning means making money

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of accepted

explanation.surface: A classy record brings in cash, though it was not well received initially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives A, the first letter of accepted, and 'not' removes it from EARNING to leave ERNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Discerning means showing good judgement and refined taste.

clue.text: But this city ain't in Pennsylvania!

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
ain't is slang for is not, so the setter takes its verb is

explanation.surface: A protest that a city with a famous tower is not in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke: as wordplay the city would be IS in PA, but the clue says it ain't, since the real place is in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisa is the Tuscan city of the Leaning Tower.

clue.text: Expedition heading off shortly on a distant island

indicators.note: heading off means taking the start, so the opening letter of shortly is used

parts.note: afar means at a distance, far away
I is the standard abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: A party of explorers sets out soon for a remote island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' gives S, the first letter of shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an overland journey, especially to observe or hunt wild animals in Africa.

clue.text: The person in the chair may be of no practical importance

definitions.meaning: a holder of a university chair, a professor
purely theoretical, as in the point is moot

explanation.definitionFit: A university scholar is one sense; a merely theoretical question is the other.

clue.text: It could describe a nurse, but never does

definitions.text: It could describe a nurse, but never does

parts.words: It could describe a nurse, but never does
parts.note: an adjective that can go before nurse for a man in that job, yet can never apply to does, the she-deer

explanation.definitionFit: The word for the masculine sex qualifies some nurses but no hind deer.

clue.text: English poet going round to get doctor

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the poet's name surrounds the letter

parts.note: A. E. Housman was the English poet of A Shropshire Lad

explanation.surface: An English poet goes on his rounds to fetch a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts E inside HOUSMAN. In Britain a houseman is a junior hospital doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage this is a junior doctor living in or working at a hospital.

clue.text: Captured by African. I'm a lion, possibly

definitions.text: Captured by African. I'm a lion, possibly

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: A lion boasts that it was caught by an African.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is held in africAN I'M A Lion, and the whole clue defines it: a lion is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion is one example of a beast, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Which Marryat hero inherits a fortune? Careful!

definitions.text: Which Marryat hero inherits a fortune
definitions.meaning: Captain Marryat's novel Mr Midshipman Easy has a hero named Easy; the question asks which hero does inherit

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a call for caution, and also answers the question, with the verb standing for inherit.
